market_context.summary: Saturday run: US cash equities and futures are closed, so every equity price here is the Friday 2026-11-13 close — the freshest honest price, not a stale one. The regime is dispersion, not direction. SPY closed 754.37, below its 759.02 SMA20 and 764.43 SMA50 and -3.49% off its 90-day high, with ATR14 at 12.77 = 1.69% of price. Friday itself opened at the high (760.07) and sold all day to close 754.37, down only 0.36% — but underneath it was a rotation, not a selloff: XLP +1.42%, XLC +1.05%, XLE +0.98%, XLF +0.81% against XLK -2.01% and SMH -2.99%. Drawdowns off the 150-session high tell the same story: SMH -27.55%, GLD -20.78%, IWM -9.06%, SPY -3.49%, XLF -2.27%, XLP -1.12%. The mechanism is the long end, not growth: the 10y is 5.10% against an effective fed funds rate of 3.88% and unemployment of 4.1%, so this is term premium repricing, and the confirmation that it is liquidity rather than a growth scare is that equities, gold AND crypto fell together — a growth scare bids bonds and gold. Crypto is in an outright bear market: BTC $67,235 (-2.97% in 24h), and the IBIT proxy is -45.78% from its two-year high, below its 200-day, on five consecutive lower closes. Money is leaving long-duration growth for short-duration cash flow, which is the correct response to a 5.10% 10y, and both of today's new ideas sit on that side of the trade.

recommendations.thesis: Conagra trades at 8.56x trailing ADJUSTED EPS (GAAP trailing EPS is -3.98; see the valuation anchor) — 14.73 against 1.72 of trailing earnings, being the 0.41, 0.47, 0.39 and 0.45 it actually reported in the four quarters to 2026-09-30 — and the Street has capitulated on it: 0 strong buy, 1 buy, 14 hold, 8 sell and 2 strong sell, a 4.0% bullish share and ten sell ratings against one buy. Three of those four quarters beat and the most recent beat by 43.9% (0.41 against a 0.285 estimate), so the earnings erosion those ten sell ratings price is forecast, not observed. An insider bought 35,000 shares on the open market at 14.5895 on 2026-07-17 — $510,632, against zero insider sales in six months — and the stock is 14.73, so the position is still available at his price. Target 19.48 is 11.3x the same trailing 1.72 and sits at the 19.475 March 2026 high where supply resumes, rather than past it: (19.48 - 14.40) / (14.40 - 12.40) = 5.08 / 2.00 = 2.54, still clearing the 2.5 long-term floor - which is the point of pulling it in. The idea did not need the stretch.
recommendations.key_risk: The ten sell ratings are not stupid. The bear case is structural — GLP-1 drugs reducing centre-store food volumes and private label taking shelf share, against a balance sheet with real leverage — and a dividend cut is how this thesis breaks fastest, because much of the holder base owns it for the yield. The 12.40 bear case is 8.5x an EPS eroded 15% to 1.46 and sits below both observed lows, 12.53 (June 2026) and 12.88 (October); a dividend cut would take it through that. RED TEAM: the dividend risk is now quantified rather than named. The declared annual dividend is 1.4012 - 89.5% of the 1.72 adjusted EPS this entire thesis is built on, a 9.55% trailing yield on 14.73, against an indicated forward yield of 4.91%, i.e. the fetched data itself implies the trailing rate is not expected to continue. Total debt to equity is 1.21x. So a cut is not the tail risk here, it is close to what the yield is already quoting. The trade does not require the dividend to survive - the thesis is the multiple - but anyone sizing this as an income position is taking a different risk than the one argued above.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case against is that 8.56x is not cheap but correct — the market pays a low multiple for an earnings stream it expects to shrink, and a value trap looks exactly like this. What answers it is the direction of the actual prints rather than an argument: three of the last four quarters beat and the latest beat by 43.9%. What does NOT answer it is the analyst split, which has been frozen at 0/1/14/8/2 for four straight months — that is stale sentiment, not improving sentiment, and it is not counted as a tailwind here. RED TEAM: the beat argument is thinner than it reads. The 43.9% beat is measured against a consensus cut to 0.285 from the 0.4619 standing a quarter earlier, and the other two beats are 1.8% and 2.1% - in line, not beats in any economic sense. So the record is one beat against a slashed bar plus three in-line prints, which is consistent with erosion being modelled ahead of time, not with erosion failing to arrive. The 15-month tape argues the same way: 29.46 in November 2024 to 14.73 now, every rally lower - 20.32 February, 19.48 March, 16.74 August, 15.54 November - so 'basing and turning up into the 200-day' is a base inside a two-year 50% decline. None of that kills the idea, and the insider, the multiple and XLP leadership all stand. It is why this is a conviction 4 and not a 5.
